<!--
============================================================================
CCP_FIRE_V11.Rmd

V11 fixes two execution issues encountered after V10 successfully completed the
nearest-neighbour distance stages. First, RStudio's interactive chunk runner
repeatedly tried to evaluate chunk-header expressions such as
`eval=cfg$use_chirps` in an environment where `cfg` was not visible, producing
spurious `object 'cfg' not found` errors even though the chunk bodies continued
to run. V11 removes configuration expressions from chunk headers and performs
the same conditions inside ordinary R code. Second, the GeoTIFF export used
base `pmax()` on a terra SpatRaster, which is not a supported raster operation
and failed with `invalid 'x' type in 'x || y'`. V11 replaces that denominator
with a terra-native `ifel()` operation. Scientific definitions, the 100 m
distance densification, the RANN/FNN/nabor functional backend preflight, the
0.05 degree analysis grid, and all outputs are unchanged.

V10 fixes the nearest-neighbour backend failure encountered in V9.
  V9 selected nabor solely because it was installed and called the Rcpp-module
  WKNND$query method without its documented radius argument. On this machine
  that method dispatch failed only after 1,776,213 road reference vertices had
  already been generated. V10 performs a tiny functional self-test before any
  expensive spatial processing, prefers RANN and then FNN, and uses nabor only
  as a tested fallback with the complete query signature (including radius=0).
  Every backend is normalised to return the same plain integer index matrix.
  The road query releases the k-d-tree/reference metric copy as soon as the
  neighbour indices have been obtained, and the peat-edge workflow uses the
  same centrally tested backend. The 100 m densification and scientific
  definitions are unchanged.

V9 removes an optional sf dependency that is not installed on this machine.
  sf::st_segmentize() on geographic coordinates dispatches to lwgeom, which
  needs liblwgeom and errored with "package lwgeom required". The line
  densification is now done directly on the coordinate matrix by linear
  interpolation in lon/lat. Over segments capped at 100 m that is
  indistinguishable from geodesic interpolation, and it needs nothing beyond
  sf and base R. Nothing else changed.

V8 fixed a regression introduced in V7 and removes a multi-hour bottleneck.

  1  The stronger cache check added in V7 called terra::readValues() without
     terra::readStart(). Every cached product therefore reported
     "[readValues] the file is not open for reading", was declared invalid,
     and was rebuilt; worse, discard_if_invalid() then deleted correct files.
     readStart/readStop are now used, and the deletion path only removes a
     file that is absent, implausibly small, or impossible to open. A layer
     or geometry mismatch is reported and the file is left alone, because the
     rebuild overwrites it anyway.

  2  The vector distance rasters now use a densify-plus-k-d-tree method by
     default. terra::distance() against a 63,000 feature road layer is
     roughly cells times features geodesic segment tests and runs for hours;
     the new method takes seconds. Its maximum absolute error is half the
     densification interval, 50 m at the default, on a covariate measured in
     kilometres over 5.5 km cells. Set cfg$distance_method = "exact" to use
     the strip-wise terra path instead. A sidecar .method file records how
     each cached raster was built so the four covariates can never end up
     mixing definitions.

  3  sweep_temp() no longer calls terra::tmpFiles(), which could not work
     with a custom tempdir and emitted a warning at every stage.

V7 fixed a fatal native crash and keeps every V6 memory protection.

The crash
  V6 aborted the whole R session, not with an R error but with a native
  abort, at "building the peat edge distance raster at 100 m". The cause is
  terra::distance(x) applied to a SpatRaster whose non-NA cells are the
  targets. That form of the function is not a chunked operation. terra has to
  hold the entire grid, plus its working structures, in RAM at once, and it
  builds them in C++ before anything is written, so the filename argument
  cannot help. The 100 m domain is about 7,700 by 10,100 cells, roughly 78
  million, and the target set is the whole peat boundary. On an 8 GB machine
  the allocation fails inside C++, and an unhandled allocation failure
  terminates the process. try() and tryCatch() operate at the R level and
  never get a chance to run, which is exactly what was observed.

What V7 does instead
  The same variable is computed by an exact streaming nearest-neighbour
  method that never holds more than one horizontal slab of the 100 m grid:
    1  one streaming pass over the CongoPeat raster with a one row halo
       extracts the coordinates of every inner boundary cell of the peat
       swamp forest class, using an 8-connected test identical to
       terra::boundaries(inner = TRUE, directions = 8)
    2  those edge coordinates go into a k-d tree
    3  a second pass walks the 100 m grid slab by slab, finds the nearest
       edge points for every cell, and converts to true geodesic metres
    4  the analysis grid mean is accumulated during the same pass
  No step ever allocates a full domain array in C++, and there is no longer
  any code path that attempts the dangerous full-domain terra::distance().

  The four vector distance rasters (roads, major roads, rivers, settlements)
  and the ones built for the grid-size robustness analysis are now computed
  in horizontal strips and written straight to disk, so no single terra call
  sees the whole grid.

  Cached products are validated against CRS, extent, resolution, layer count,
  readable values and a plausible file size before reuse, and any file that
  fails is deleted and rebuilt rather than trusted.

Everything from V6 is preserved: memfrac 0.35, the scratch directory at
~/terra_tmp_ccp outside the project and outside cloud storage, disk-backed
Hansen processing through a VRT, the streaming count engine, cached reusable
products in data/processed/, targeted rm() and gc(), no parallelism, the
restartable design, the progress messages, the directory layout, and the
400 dpi PNG plus PDF publication outputs.

The science is unchanged. See the note on d_peat_edge_km in the peat edge
section for the one implementation detail worth recording in the methods.

V6 was a memory-optimised rewrite of V5 for an 8 GB Apple Silicon Mac.
The science is unchanged: same domain, same 0.00025 degree analytical
resolution, same 0.05 degree analysis grid, same years, same variables,
same models, same robustness analyses, same outputs. Only the execution
strategy changed.

What changed, and why
  1  terra memfrac lowered to 0.35 and the terra scratch directory moved to
     ~/terra_tmp_ccp on the internal SSD, outside the project and outside
     any cloud-synchronised folder. A startup guard refuses to run if the
     scratch path resolves inside the project or a known cloud folder.
  2  Hansen and fire mosaics are assembled through a GDAL VRT rather than by
     reading tiles into terra. A VRT copies no pixels, so four 600 MB tiles
     never coexist in RAM. Crop and mask are then streamed straight to a
     compressed file.
  3  The single largest change: grid counts and the 2001-2025 annual counts
     are produced by one streaming block pass over the 30 m grid instead of
     roughly one hundred whole-raster terra passes. V5 built five- and
     four-layer stacks of derived 986-million-cell rasters, each of which
     terra materialised as an uncompressed double-precision temporary file.
     That is what filled RAM and filled terra_tmp. The block engine reads
     100 raster rows at a time, tabulates every year and every metric from
     that slab, and keeps only small accumulator arrays. Peak RAM for this
     stage is a few hundred MB.
  4  The block engine is verified against terra::aggregate on an aligned
     sub-window before it is trusted, and there is an automatic fallback to
     a year-by-year, file-backed terra path if verification fails.
  5  The canopy-threshold sensitivity is one streaming pass instead of
     twelve whole-raster passes, using exact per-row geodesic pixel areas.
  6  The stratified validation sample no longer calls terra::cells() on a
     986-million-cell mask, which would have returned hundreds of millions
     of cell indices. It uses probability-proportional-to-size selection of
     analysis cells followed by uniform selection inside the chosen cell,
     which is uniform over the stratum and reads only small windows.
  7  Distance rasters, OSM subsets, the peat class frequency table and every
     expensive intermediate are cached in data/processed/ and validated
     before reuse.
  8  Large data frames are released as soon as the last chunk that needs
     them has run. Every rm() was checked against downstream chunks.
  9  Every figure and every map is written as 400 dpi PNG and as PDF,
     directly into outputs/figures/ and outputs/maps/.

Directory layout is unchanged:
  ccp_fire/data/{raw,processed,manual_inputs}
  ccp_fire/outputs/{tables,figures,maps,geotiff,diagnostics}
Disposable terra scratch files live outside the project, in ~/terra_tmp_ccp.

Purpose
  Quantify how much of the mapped forest loss in the central Congo Basin
  peatland complex (Republic of the Congo and Democratic Republic of the
  Congo) between 2001 and 2025 was attributable to fire, test whether the
  fire-attributed share rose in 2023-2025, and identify where fire-driven
  loss is concentrated relative to peat swamp forest, protected areas,
  roads, rivers, settlements and rainfall deficit.

Design
  Unit of analysis  : 0.05 degree grid cell (about 5.5 km)
  Outcome           : count of 30 m forest-loss pixels attributed to fire
  Contrast outcome  : count of 30 m forest-loss pixels not attributed to fire
  Exposure          : peat swamp forest fraction, access, protection, rainfall
  Models            : negative binomial GLM with log(baseline forest) offset
============================================================================
-->

# Configuration

```{r config}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

cfg <- list(

  # Root directory. All inputs and outputs live below this.
  root_dir = "ccp_fire",

  # Include the DRC part of the peatland complex.
  include_drc = TRUE,

  # Study domain definition.
  # "peat_buffer" = mapped peat swamp forest plus a buffer (recommended)
  # "bbox"        = the whole CongoPeat footprint
  domain_mode      = "peat_buffer",
  domain_buffer_km = 50,

  # Analysis grid cell size in degrees. 0.05 deg is about 5.5 km at the equator
  # and divides the Hansen 0.00025 deg grid exactly (factor 200).
  grid_deg = 0.05,

  # Baseline forest definition: minimum Hansen tree canopy cover in 2000 (%).
  forest_thresh = 30,

  # Sensitivity thresholds for the same quantity.
  forest_thresh_sens = c(10, 30, 50),

  # CongoPeat simplified map class codes.
  # 1 open water, 2 savanna, 3 other tropical forest (terra firme),
  # 4 peat swamp forest
  peat_class        = 4L,
  forest_classes    = c(3L, 4L),

  # Analysis windows.
  year_min      = 2001L,
  year_max      = 2025L,
  recent_window = c(2023L, 2025L),   # the anomaly window
  base_window   = c(2001L, 2022L),   # the reference window

  # Rainfall covariate.
  use_chirps   = TRUE,
  chirps_years = 2001:2025,

  # Hansen treecover2000, needed for the canopy-threshold sensitivity.
  download_treecover2000 = TRUE,

  # Stratified validation points per stratum. Set to 0 to skip.
  n_validation_per_stratum = 100L,

  # Random seed.
  seed = 20260908L,

  # Alternative grid sizes used in the robustness analysis.
  grid_deg_sens = c(0.025, 0.05, 0.1),

  # ---- memory and execution settings, new in V6 --------------------------

  # Fraction of RAM terra may use. 0.35 on an 8 GB machine leaves headroom
  # for R, RStudio and macOS. Reliability matters more than speed here.
  terra_memfrac = 0.35,

  # Disposable terra scratch directory. Must be on the internal SSD and must
  # not be inside the project or any cloud-synchronised folder.
  terra_tmp_dir = path.expand("~/terra_tmp_ccp"),

  # Raster rows read per slab in the streaming block engine. 100 rows of a
  # 36000 column raster is about 29 MB per layer, four layers per read.
  block_rows_target = 100L,

  # Verify the block engine against terra::aggregate on an aligned window
  # before trusting it. Cheap, and it catches any indexing error.
  verify_block_engine = TRUE,
  verify_window_cells = 6L,

  # Remove terra scratch files left by earlier sessions at startup.
  purge_stale_terra_tmp = TRUE,

  # How the vector distance rasters (roads, rivers, settlements) are computed.
  # "fast"  = densify the lines to distance_vertex_m, then nearest-vertex
  #           search with a k-d tree and a geodesic recomputation. Seconds
  #           per layer. Maximum absolute error is half the densification
  #           interval, so 50 m at the default, on a covariate measured in
  #           kilometres over 5.5 km cells.
  # "exact" = terra::distance() against the full vector, in strips. Exact to
  #           the segment, but many hours for a 63,000 feature road layer.
  distance_method   = "fast",
  distance_vertex_m = 100,

  # Keep the full 100 m peat edge distance raster as a reusable product in
  # data/processed/. It is about 150 to 300 MB compressed. Set FALSE to
  # compute the analysis grid covariate without keeping the 100 m layer.
  write_peat_edge_100m = TRUE
)

# Derived directories. The layout is unchanged from V5.
cfg$data_dir    <- file.path(cfg$root_dir, "data")
cfg$raw_dir     <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "raw")
cfg$proc_dir    <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "processed")
cfg$out_dir     <- file.path(cfg$root_dir, "outputs")
cfg$tab_dir     <- file.path(cfg$out_dir, "tables")
cfg$fig_dir     <- file.path(cfg$out_dir, "figures")
cfg$map_dir     <- file.path(cfg$out_dir, "maps")
cfg$tif_dir     <- file.path(cfg$out_dir, "geotiff")
cfg$diag_dir    <- file.path(cfg$out_dir, "diagnostics")
cfg$manual_dir  <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "manual_inputs")

for (d in c(cfg$root_dir, cfg$data_dir, cfg$raw_dir, cfg$proc_dir,
            cfg$out_dir, cfg$tab_dir, cfg$fig_dir, cfg$map_dir,
            cfg$tif_dir, cfg$diag_dir, cfg$manual_dir)) {
  dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
}

set.seed(cfg$seed)
options(timeout = max(7200, getOption("timeout")))
str(cfg[!names(cfg) %in% c("chirps_years")])
```

```{r packages}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Nearest-neighbour backend preflight
#
# V9 selected nabor only because it was installed. Its WKNND Rcpp-module query
# was then called without the documented radius argument and failed after the
# expensive road densification had already completed. V10 tests the exact
# build/query path on a tiny matrix before any expensive spatial processing.
# The preferred order on this Mac is RANN, FNN, then a verified nabor fallback.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

nn_normalize_indices <- function(idx, nq, k, nref, backend) {
  nq <- as.integer(nq); k <- as.integer(k); nref <- as.integer(nref)

  # Only coerce ordinary atomic/data-frame outputs. Never dispatch as.matrix()
  # on an arbitrary backend/Rcpp object.
  if (is.data.frame(idx)) idx <- as.matrix(idx)
  if (is.atomic(idx) && is.null(dim(idx))) {
    if (length(idx) != nq * k) {
      stop("Nearest-neighbour backend ", backend, " returned ", length(idx),
           " indices; expected ", nq * k, ".")
    }
    idx <- matrix(idx, nrow = nq, ncol = k)
  } else if (!is.matrix(idx)) {
    stop("Nearest-neighbour backend ", backend,
         " returned an unsupported object of class ",
         paste(class(idx), collapse = "/"), ".")
  }

  if (!is.numeric(idx) && !is.integer(idx)) {
    stop("Nearest-neighbour backend ", backend,
         " did not return numeric/integer indices.")
  }
  if (length(dim(idx)) != 2L || any(dim(idx) != c(nq, k))) {
    if (length(idx) == nq * k) {
      dim(idx) <- c(nq, k)
    } else {
      stop("Nearest-neighbour backend ", backend, " returned dimensions ",
           paste(dim(idx), collapse = " x "), "; expected ", nq, " x ", k, ".")
    }
  }
  if (anyNA(idx) || any(!is.finite(idx)) || any(idx < 1) || any(idx > nref)) {
    stop("Nearest-neighbour backend ", backend,
         " returned missing, non-finite or out-of-range indices.")
  }
  storage.mode(idx) <- "integer"
  idx
}

nn_index_builder <- function(ref_xy, backend) {
  if (is.data.frame(ref_xy)) ref_xy <- as.matrix(ref_xy)
  if (!is.matrix(ref_xy) || ncol(ref_xy) != 2L || !is.numeric(ref_xy)) {
    stop("Nearest-neighbour reference coordinates must be a numeric two-column matrix.")
  }
  storage.mode(ref_xy) <- "double"
  if (!nrow(ref_xy) || any(!is.finite(ref_xy))) {
    stop("Nearest-neighbour reference coordinates are empty or non-finite.")
  }
  nref <- nrow(ref_xy)

  prepare_query <- function(q, k) {
    if (is.data.frame(q)) q <- as.matrix(q)
    if (!is.matrix(q) || ncol(q) != 2L || !is.numeric(q)) {
      stop("Nearest-neighbour query coordinates must be a numeric two-column matrix.")
    }
    storage.mode(q) <- "double"
    if (!nrow(q) || any(!is.finite(q))) {
      stop("Nearest-neighbour query coordinates are empty or non-finite.")
    }
    kk <- max(1L, min(as.integer(k), nref))
    list(q = q, k = kk)
  }

  if (identical(backend, "RANN")) {
    if (!requireNamespace("RANN", quietly = TRUE)) stop("RANN is not installed.")
    return(list(
      backend = "RANN",
      query = function(q, k) {
        z <- prepare_query(q, k)
        raw <- RANN::nn2(data = ref_xy, query = z$q, k = z$k,
                         treetype = "kd", searchtype = "standard")$nn.idx
        nn_normalize_indices(raw, nrow(z$q), z$k, nref, "RANN")
      }
    ))
  }

  if (identical(backend, "FNN")) {
    if (!requireNamespace("FNN", quietly = TRUE)) stop("FNN is not installed.")
    return(list(
      backend = "FNN",
      query = function(q, k) {
        z <- prepare_query(q, k)
        raw <- FNN::get.knnx(data = ref_xy, query = z$q, k = z$k,
                             algorithm = "kd_tree")$nn.index
        nn_normalize_indices(raw, nrow(z$q), z$k, nref, "FNN")
      }
    ))
  }

  if (identical(backend, "nabor")) {
    if (!requireNamespace("nabor", quietly = TRUE)) stop("nabor is not installed.")
    # nabor's documented WKNND query signature is query(query, k, eps, radius).
    # V9 omitted radius, which can make Rcpp-module method dispatch fail.
    tr <- nabor::WKNND(ref_xy)
    return(list(
      backend = "nabor",
      query = function(q, k) {
        z <- prepare_query(q, k)
        ans <- tr$query(z$q, k = z$k, eps = 0, radius = 0)
        if (!is.list(ans) || is.null(ans$nn.idx)) {
          stop("nabor WKNND$query did not return a list containing nn.idx.")
        }
        nn_normalize_indices(ans$nn.idx, nrow(z$q), z$k, nref, "nabor")
      }
    ))
  }

  stop("Unsupported nearest-neighbour backend: ", backend)
}

nn_backend_self_test <- function(backend) {
  ref <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(10, 0), c(0, 10), c(10, 10), c(5, 5))
  qry <- rbind(c(0.1, 0.2), c(9.8, 0.1), c(9.9, 9.9))
  storage.mode(ref) <- "double"
  storage.mode(qry) <- "double"
  expected_first <- c(1L, 2L, 4L)

  err <- NULL
  ok <- tryCatch({
    nn <- nn_index_builder(ref, backend = backend)
    idx <- nn$query(qry, 2L)
    good <- is.matrix(idx) && is.integer(idx) &&
      all(dim(idx) == c(nrow(qry), 2L)) &&
      all(idx >= 1L & idx <= nrow(ref)) &&
      identical(as.integer(idx[, 1]), expected_first)
    rm(nn, idx); gc()
    if (!good) stop("returned indices failed the dimension/range/nearest-point checks")
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    err <<- conditionMessage(e)
    FALSE
  })

  if (isTRUE(ok)) {
    message("Nearest-neighbour backend ", backend, ": OK")
  } else {
    message("Nearest-neighbour backend ", backend,
            ": FAILED functional test (", err, ")")
  }
  isTRUE(ok)
}

select_nn_backend <- function() {
  # Prefer a plain-function backend on this machine. If neither RANN nor FNN is
  # installed, try RANN first. If it cannot be installed or fails its functional
  # test, try FNN. nabor is retained only as an explicitly verified fallback.
  if (!requireNamespace("RANN", quietly = TRUE) &&
      !requireNamespace("FNN", quietly = TRUE)) {
    message("Installing RANN for the nearest-neighbour backend preflight.")
    try(install.packages("RANN", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org"), silent = TRUE)
  }

  if (requireNamespace("RANN", quietly = TRUE) && nn_backend_self_test("RANN")) {
    return("RANN")
  }

  if (!requireNamespace("FNN", quietly = TRUE)) {
    message("RANN is unavailable or failed its self-test; installing FNN.")
    try(install.packages("FNN", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org"), silent = TRUE)
  }
  if (requireNamespace("FNN", quietly = TRUE) && nn_backend_self_test("FNN")) {
    return("FNN")
  }

  if (requireNamespace("nabor", quietly = TRUE) && nn_backend_self_test("nabor")) {
    message("Using nabor only because its corrected WKNND path passed the functional test.")
    return("nabor")
  }

  stop(
    "No tested nearest-neighbour backend is usable. Try one of:\n",
    "  install.packages(\"RANN\", repos=\"https://cloud.r-project.org\")\n",
    "  install.packages(\"FNN\", repos=\"https://cloud.r-project.org\")\n",
    "Then restart R and rerun the script."
  )
}

.nn_backend_selected <- select_nn_backend()
message("Using nearest-neighbour backend: ", .nn_backend_selected)

# dplyr::select must win over MASS::select
select <- dplyr::select

sessionInfo()$R.version$version.string
```

# terra scratch directory and preflight checks

The scratch directory holds disposable terra temporaries only. Reusable
processed products stay in `data/processed/` and are never deleted here.

```{r terra-setup}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Locate a safe scratch directory on the internal SSD
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

cloud_markers <- c(
  "Library/CloudStorage", "Mobile Documents", "com~apple~CloudDocs",
  "iCloud", "Dropbox", "OneDrive", "Google Drive", "GoogleDrive",
  "Proton Drive", "ProtonDrive", "pCloud", "Box Sync", "Creative Cloud",
  "Sync.com", "MEGA", "Nextcloud", "ownCloud"
)

path_looks_cloudy <- function(p) {
  pn <- normalizePath(p, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
  any(vapply(cloud_markers, function(m) grepl(m, pn, fixed = TRUE), logical(1)))
}

local_tmp <- cfg$terra_tmp_dir
dir.create(local_tmp, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!dir.exists(local_tmp)) {
  stop("Could not create the terra scratch directory at ", local_tmp)
}

local_tmp_norm   <- normalizePath(local_tmp,     winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
project_norm     <- normalizePath(cfg$root_dir,  winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

if (startsWith(local_tmp_norm, project_norm)) {
  stop("The terra scratch directory resolves inside the project (", local_tmp_norm,
       "). Set cfg$terra_tmp_dir to a path outside ", project_norm)
}
if (path_looks_cloudy(local_tmp_norm)) {
  stop("The terra scratch directory looks cloud-synchronised (", local_tmp_norm,
       "). Set cfg$terra_tmp_dir to a plain local path such as ~/terra_tmp_ccp")
}

# Write test, because a path can exist and still be read-only or offloaded.
probe <- file.path(local_tmp_norm, ".write_probe")
ok_write <- tryCatch({ writeLines("ok", probe); file.exists(probe) },
                     error = function(e) FALSE)
unlink(probe)
if (!isTRUE(ok_write)) stop("The terra scratch directory is not writable: ", local_tmp_norm)

terra::terraOptions(
  memfrac  = cfg$terra_memfrac,
  tempdir  = local_tmp_norm,
  progress = 1
)

# Confirm terra actually took the setting, rather than assuming it did.
terra_tmp_actual <- terra::terraOptions(print = FALSE)$tempdir
message("terra tempdir in use: ", terra_tmp_actual)
message("terra memfrac in use: ", terra::terraOptions(print = FALSE)$memfrac)
if (!identical(normalizePath(terra_tmp_actual, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE),
               local_tmp_norm)) {
  stop("terra did not accept the scratch directory. Requested ", local_tmp_norm,
       " but terra reports ", terra_tmp_actual)
}

# Remove scratch files left behind by earlier sessions. Nothing in this
# session references them yet, so this is safe. Reusable products in
# data/processed/ are untouched.
if (isTRUE(cfg$purge_stale_terra_tmp)) {
  stale <- list.files(local_tmp_norm, pattern = "^spat.*\\.(tif|vrt|json|aux\\.xml)$",
                      full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(stale)) {
    message("Removing ", length(stale), " stale terra scratch files (",
            round(sum(file.info(stale)$size, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6), " MB)")
    unlink(stale)
  }
  invisible(try(terra::tmpFiles(current = FALSE, orphan = TRUE, old = TRUE,
                                remove = TRUE), silent = TRUE))
}

# The V5 scratch folder inside the project is no longer used. Report it so it
# can be deleted by hand; nothing is removed automatically inside the project.
old_tmp <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "terra_tmp")
old_tmp2 <- file.path(cfg$root_dir, "terra_tmp")
for (p in c(old_tmp, old_tmp2)) {
  if (dir.exists(p)) {
    fs_ <- list.files(p, full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
    message("Obsolete scratch folder still present: ", p, " (", length(fs_),
            " files, ", round(sum(file.info(fs_)$size, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6),
            " MB). It is no longer used and can be deleted manually.")
  }
}
```

```{r preflight}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Preflight report

free_mb <- function(path) {
  out <- tryCatch(system2("df", c("-Pk", shQuote(path)), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE),
                  error = function(e) NULL, warning = function(w) NULL)
  if (is.null(out) || length(out) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  f <- strsplit(trimws(out[2]), "\\s+")[[1]]
  if (length(f) < 4) return(NA_real_)
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(f[4]) / 1024)
}

    paste(sum(dir.exists(expected_dirs)), "of", length(expected_dirs))
  )
)
```

# Helper functions

Downloading, integrity checking, cached raster products, and the disk-backed
write helpers used throughout.

```{r helpers}
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (!is.null(a) && length(a) && !all(is.na(a))) a else b

msg <- function(...) message(format(Sys.time(), "[%H:%M:%S] "), ...)

# Registry of files produced, used by the final summary.
.outputs <- character(0)
register_output <- function(p) {
  .outputs <<- unique(c(.outputs, p))
  invisible(p)
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Downloads
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

curl_available <- Sys.which("curl") != ""

curl_download <- function(url, dest, resume = TRUE) {
  if (!curl_available) {
    utils::download.file(url, destfile = dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
    return(0L)
  }
  args <- c(
    "-L", "--fail", "--silent", "--show-error",
    "--http1.1",
    "--retry", "20", "--retry-delay", "10", "--retry-all-errors",
    "--connect-timeout", "60",
    "--speed-limit", "1024", "--speed-time", "60"
  )
  if (resume) args <- c(args, "-C", "-")
  args <- c(args, "-o", normalizePath(dest, mustWork = FALSE), url)
  invisible(system2("curl", args))
}

get_content_length <- function(url) {
  tryCatch({
    r <- httr2::request(url) |>
      httr2::req_method("HEAD") |>
      httr2::req_timeout(90) |>
      httr2::req_perform()
    cl <- httr2::resp_header(r, "content-length")
    if (is.null(cl) || is.na(cl) || cl == "") NA_real_ else as.numeric(cl)
  }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

download_resumable <- function(url, dest, rounds = 40, min_bytes = 1024) {
  expected <- get_content_length(url)
  if (is.na(expected)) msg("Server did not report a size for ", basename(dest),
                           ". Falling back to a validity check only.")
  for (i in seq_len(rounds)) {
    have <- if (file.exists(dest)) as.numeric(file.info(dest)$size) else 0
    if (!is.na(expected) && have >= expected) break
    msg(sprintf("resume round %d/%d for %s: have %.1f MB%s",
                i, rounds, basename(dest), have / 1e6,
                if (is.na(expected)) "" else sprintf(" of %.1f MB", expected / 1e6)))
    curl_download(url, dest, resume = have > 0)
    Sys.sleep(2)
    now <- if (file.exists(dest)) as.numeric(file.info(dest)$size) else 0
    if (now <= have && i > 3) {
      msg("No progress on ", basename(dest), ". Restarting the transfer.")
      unlink(dest)
    }
  }
  if (!file.exists(dest) || as.numeric(file.info(dest)$size) < min_bytes) {
    stop("Could not download after ", rounds, " resume rounds: ", url)
  }
  if (!is.na(expected) && as.numeric(file.info(dest)$size) < expected) {
    stop("Incomplete after ", rounds, " resume rounds (",
         round(file.info(dest)$size / 1e6), " of ", round(expected / 1e6), " MB): ", url)
  }
  dest
}

url_exists <- function(url) {
  tryCatch({
    r <- httr2::request(url) |>
      httr2::req_method("HEAD") |>
      httr2::req_timeout(60) |>
      httr2::req_error(is_error = function(resp) FALSE) |>
      httr2::req_perform()
    httr2::resp_status(r) < 400
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
}

validate_geotiff <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path) || file.info(path)$size < 2048) return(FALSE)
  ok <- tryCatch({
    r <- terra::rast(path)
    terra::readStart(r)
    on.exit(terra::readStop(r), add = TRUE)
    nr <- min(64L, terra::nrow(r)); nc <- min(64L, terra::ncol(r))
    v <- terra::readValues(r, row = 1, nrows = nr, col = 1, ncols = nc)
    !is.null(v)
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  isTRUE(ok)
}

# Stronger reuse test for cached processed products: open, and check geometry
# against a reference raster and an expected layer count. This is what stops
# the workflow silently reusing an incomplete or wrongly aligned product.
cached_ok <- function(path, ref = NULL, nlyr = NULL, min_bytes = 1024,
                      label = basename(path)) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(FALSE)
  sz <- as.numeric(file.info(path)$size)
  if (is.na(sz) || sz < min_bytes) {
    msg("cached ", label, " is only ", ifelse(is.na(sz), "unreadable", round(sz)),
        " bytes, which is implausible. It will be rebuilt.")
    return(FALSE)
  }
  if (!validate_geotiff(path)) {
    msg("cached ", label, " could not be opened or read. It will be rebuilt.")
    return(FALSE)
  }
  ok <- tryCatch({
    r <- terra::rast(path)
    good <- TRUE
    if (!is.null(nlyr) && terra::nlyr(r) != nlyr) {
      msg("cached ", label, " has ", terra::nlyr(r), " layers, expected ", nlyr,
          ". It will be rebuilt.")
      good <- FALSE
    }
    if (good && (is.na(terra::crs(r)) || !nzchar(terra::crs(r)))) {
      msg("cached ", label, " has no CRS. It will be rebuilt.")
      good <- FALSE
    }
    if (good && !is.null(ref)) {
      # compareGeom checks extent, resolution, dimensions and CRS together.
      if (!terra::compareGeom(r, ref, stopOnError = FALSE, messages = FALSE)) {
        msg("cached ", label, " does not match the reference CRS, extent or ",
            "resolution. It will be rebuilt.")
        good <- FALSE
      }
    }
    if (good) {
      # A truncated GeoTIFF often opens but fails on the last block, so read
      # the bottom of the file as well as the top.
      #
      # readValues() needs an explicit readStart(). Omitting it in V7 made
      # every cached product report "[readValues] the file is not open for
      # reading", so every product was declared invalid and rebuilt, and
      # discard_if_invalid() deleted good files. That is fixed here.
      nr <- terra::nrow(r)
      terra::readStart(r)
      v <- try(terra::readValues(r, row = max(1L, nr - 1L), nrows = min(2L, nr),
                                 col = 1, ncols = min(64L, terra::ncol(r))),
               silent = TRUE)
      try(terra::readStop(r), silent = TRUE)
      if (inherits(v, "try-error") || is.null(v) || !length(v)) good <- FALSE
    }
    good
  }, error = function(e) {
    msg("cached ", label, " failed validation (", conditionMessage(e),
        "). It will be rebuilt.")
    FALSE
  })
  if (isTRUE(ok)) msg("reusing cached product: ", label)
  isTRUE(ok)
}

# Delete a cached or scratch raster that does not pass validation. Only the
# named file is removed; reusable products that are valid are never touched.
# Delete a cached raster only when it is genuinely unusable: absent from disk,
# implausibly small, or impossible to open and read. A layer count or geometry
# mismatch is reported and the file is left in place, because the rebuild
# overwrites it anyway and deleting a good file on a false negative is the
# worse failure. V7 deleted on any negative result, which combined with the
# readValues bug above destroyed correct products.
discard_if_invalid <- function(path, min_bytes = 1024, label = basename(path)) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(invisible(FALSE))
  sz <- as.numeric(file.info(path)$size)
  unusable <- is.na(sz) || sz < min_bytes || !validate_geotiff(path)
  if (!unusable) return(invisible(TRUE))
  msg("removing damaged or unreadable file: ", path)
  unlink(path); unlink(paste0(path, ".aux.xml"))
  invisible(FALSE)
}

download_geotiff_safe <- function(url, dest, tries = 3) {
  if (file.exists(dest) && validate_geotiff(dest)) {
    exp <- get_content_length(url)
    if (is.na(exp) || identical(as.numeric(file.info(dest)$size), exp)) {
      msg("cached and valid: ", basename(dest))
      return(dest)
    }
  }
  expected <- get_content_length(url)
  for (i in seq_len(tries)) {
    msg(sprintf("download attempt %d/%d: %s", i, tries, basename(dest)))
    if (!file.exists(dest)) curl_download(url, dest, resume = FALSE)
    else                    curl_download(url, dest, resume = TRUE)
    if (!is.na(expected)) {
      actual <- file.info(dest)$size
      if (!identical(as.numeric(actual), expected)) {
        msg(sprintf("size mismatch for %s (%.0f vs %.0f). Refetching from scratch.",
                    basename(dest), actual, expected))
        unlink(dest); curl_download(url, dest, resume = FALSE)
      }
    }
    if (validate_geotiff(dest)) return(dest)
    msg("GeoTIFF failed to open. Deleting and retrying.")
    unlink(dest); Sys.sleep(3)
  }
  stop("Could not obtain a valid GeoTIFF after ", tries, " attempts: ", url)
}

download_file_safe <- function(url, dest, tries = 3, min_bytes = 1024) {
  if (file.exists(dest) && file.info(dest)$size >= min_bytes) {
    msg("cached: ", basename(dest)); return(dest)
  }
  for (i in seq_len(tries)) {
    msg(sprintf("download attempt %d/%d: %s", i, tries, basename(dest)))
    try(curl_download(url, dest, resume = file.exists(dest)), silent = TRUE)
    if (file.exists(dest) && file.info(dest)$size >= min_bytes) return(dest)
    unlink(dest); Sys.sleep(3)
  }
  stop("Could not download: ", url)
}

is_zip_file <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path) || file.info(path)$size < 4) return(FALSE)
  con <- file(path, "rb"); on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE)
  identical(readBin(con, what = "raw", n = 2), charToRaw("PK"))
}

gdrive_download <- function(file_id, dest, overwrite = FALSE) {
  if (file.exists(dest) && !overwrite && is_zip_file(dest)) return(dest)
  base <- sprintf("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=%s", file_id)
  r1 <- httr2::request(base) |>
    httr2::req_options(followlocation = TRUE) |>
    httr2::req_timeout(600) |>
    httr2::req_perform()
  ct <- tolower(httr2::resp_header(r1, "content-type") %||% "")
  body_raw <- httr2::resp_body_raw(r1)
  if (!grepl("text/html", ct)) { writeBin(body_raw, dest); return(dest) }
  html  <- rawToChar(body_raw)
  token <- stringr::str_match(html, "confirm=([0-9A-Za-z_\\-]+)")[, 2]
  if (is.na(token) || token == "") { writeBin(body_raw, dest); return(dest) }
  r2 <- httr2::request(paste0(base, "&confirm=", token)) |>
    httr2::req_options(followlocation = TRUE) |>
    httr2::req_timeout(1800) |>
    httr2::req_perform()
  writeBin(httr2::resp_body_raw(r2), dest)
  dest
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Raster utilities
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

tiles_for_bbox <- function(bbox) {
  eps <- 1e-9
  lon_w <- seq(floor((as.numeric(bbox["xmin"]) + eps) / 10) * 10,
               floor((as.numeric(bbox["xmax"]) - eps) / 10) * 10, by = 10)
  lat_l <- seq(floor((as.numeric(bbox["ymin"]) + eps) / 10) * 10,
               floor((as.numeric(bbox["ymax"]) - eps) / 10) * 10, by = 10)
  lat_u <- lat_l + 10
  lat_tag <- function(x) if (x >= 0) sprintf("%02dN", abs(x)) else sprintf("%02dS", abs(x))
  lon_tag <- function(x) if (x >= 0) sprintf("%03dE", abs(x)) else sprintf("%03dW", abs(x))
  out <- character(0)
  for (lu in lat_u) for (lw in lon_w) out <- c(out, paste0(lat_tag(lu), "_", lon_tag(lw)))
  unique(out)
}

# Standard write options. LZW keeps intermediates small, tiling keeps the
# streaming reads in the block engine cheap.
wopt_int  <- list(datatype = "INT1U", gdal = c("COMPRESS=LZW", "TILED=YES"))
wopt_flt  <- list(datatype = "FLT4S", gdal = c("COMPRESS=LZW", "TILED=YES"))

# A scratch path inside the safe terra directory, for our own intermediates.
scratch_dir <- file.path(local_tmp_norm, "scratch")
dir.create(scratch_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
scratch <- function(name) file.path(scratch_dir, name)

# Remove specific scratch files we created, once nothing references them.
drop_scratch <- function(paths) {
  paths <- paths[file.exists(paths)]
  if (length(paths)) {
    unlink(paths)
    unlink(paste0(paths, ".aux.xml"))
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Release terra temporaries between stages. Only files left by earlier R
# sessions are removed: current and orphan files are left alone, because a
# live SpatRaster may still be backed by one of them. gc() lets terra release
# its own unreferenced temporaries safely.
sweep_temp <- function() {
  gc()
  # terra::tmpFiles() can only find "old" files when terra uses the R session
  # tempdir, which it does not here, so calling it just emits a warning on
  # every stage. gc() is what actually releases terra temporaries.
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Build a GDAL VRT over a set of tiles. A VRT references the tiles rather than
# copying pixels, so four 600 MB Hansen tiles never coexist in memory.
build_vrt <- function(tile_paths, vrt_path) {
  if (!length(tile_paths)) stop("no tiles supplied for ", basename(vrt_path))
  unlink(vrt_path)
  v <- terra::vrt(tile_paths, filename = vrt_path, overwrite = TRUE)
  v
}

# Replace NA with 0, written straight to disk with a one byte datatype.
na0_to_file <- function(r, filename, wopt = wopt_int) {
  terra::ifel(is.na(r), 0, r, filename = filename, overwrite = TRUE, wopt = wopt)
}

# In-memory NA to zero, for small rasters only.
na0 <- function(r) terra::ifel(is.na(r), 0, r)

write_table <- function(x, path) {
  readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(x), path, na = "")
  msg("wrote ", path)
  register_output(path)
  invisible(path)
}

# Every figure and map is written as 400 dpi PNG and as PDF, both directly in
# the target directory. No png/ or pdf/ subdirectories are created.
save_plot_both <- function(plot, name, dir, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 400) {
  png_p <- file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".png"))
  pdf_p <- file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".pdf"))
  ggplot2::ggsave(png_p, plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi,
                  bg = "white")
  ok <- try(ggplot2::ggsave(pdf_p, plot, width = width, height = height,
                            device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, bg = "white"),
            silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(ok, "try-error")) {
    try(ggplot2::ggsave(pdf_p, plot, width = width, height = height,
                        device = "pdf", bg = "white"), silent = TRUE)
  }
  msg("wrote ", png_p, " and ", basename(pdf_p))
  register_output(png_p); register_output(pdf_p)
  invisible(c(png_p, pdf_p))
}

save_fig <- function(plot, name, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 400) {
  save_plot_both(plot, name, cfg$fig_dir, width, height, dpi)
}
save_map <- function(plot, name, width = 7.5, height = 7, dpi = 400) {
  save_plot_both(plot, name, cfg$map_dir, width, height, dpi)
}

write_tif <- function(r, path, wopt = wopt_flt) {
  terra::writeRaster(r, path, overwrite = TRUE,
                     datatype = wopt$datatype, gdal = wopt$gdal)
  msg("wrote ", path)
  register_output(path)
  invisible(path)
}

theme_paper <- ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_line(linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey88"),
    axis.title  = ggplot2::element_text(face = "plain", size = 11),
    axis.text   = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
    legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title  = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(6, 10, 6, 6),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

# Administrative boundaries

```{r admin-boundaries}
iso_list <- if (isTRUE(cfg$include_drc)) c("COG", "COD") else "COG"

get_adm1_geoboundaries <- function(iso) {
  api <- sprintf("https://www.geoboundaries.org/api/current/gbOpen/%s/ADM1/", iso)
  meta <- jsonlite::fromJSON(api)
  url  <- meta$gjDownloadURL
  if (is.null(url) || !nzchar(url)) stop("no gjDownloadURL for ", iso)
  dest <- file.path(cfg$raw_dir, sprintf("geoBoundaries_%s_ADM1.geojson", iso))
  download_file_safe(url, dest, min_bytes = 5000)
  x <- sf::st_read(dest, quiet = TRUE)
  names(x)[names(x) == "shapeName"] <- "adm1_name"
  x$iso3 <- iso
  x[, c("adm1_name", "iso3")]
}

get_adm1_gadm <- function(iso) {
  url  <- sprintf("https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/gadm/gadm4.1/gpkg/gadm41_%s.gpkg", iso)
  dest <- file.path(cfg$raw_dir, sprintf("gadm41_%s.gpkg", iso))
  download_file_safe(url, dest, min_bytes = 100000)
  lyrs <- sf::st_layers(dest)$name
  lyr  <- lyrs[grepl("_1$", lyrs)][1]
  x <- sf::st_read(dest, layer = lyr, quiet = TRUE)
  names(x)[names(x) == "NAME_1"] <- "adm1_name"
  x$iso3 <- iso
  x[, c("adm1_name", "iso3")]
}

adm1_list <- lapply(iso_list, function(iso) {
  out <- try(get_adm1_geoboundaries(iso), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(out, "try-error")) {
    msg("geoBoundaries failed for ", iso, ". Trying GADM.")
    out <- try(get_adm1_gadm(iso), silent = TRUE)
  }
  if (inherits(out, "try-error")) {
    stop("Could not obtain ADM1 boundaries for ", iso,
         ". Download gadm41_", iso, ".gpkg from https://gadm.org/download_country.html",
         " and place it in ", cfg$raw_dir)
  }
  out
})

adm1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(adm1_list, function(x) sf::st_transform(x, 4326)))
adm1 <- sf::st_make_valid(adm1)
rm(adm1_list)

countries <- adm1 |>
  dplyr::group_by(iso3) |>
  dplyr::summarise(.groups = "drop") |>
  sf::st_make_valid()

sf::write_sf(adm1,      file.path(cfg$proc_dir, "adm1.gpkg"),      delete_dsn = TRUE)
sf::write_sf(countries, file.path(cfg$proc_dir, "countries.gpkg"), delete_dsn = TRUE)

msg("ADM1 units loaded: ", nrow(adm1), " across ", paste(iso_list, collapse = ", "))
print(sf::st_bbox(countries))
```

# CongoPeat peatland map and study domain

```{r congopeat}
peat_zip <- file.path(cfg$raw_dir, "CongoPeat_SimplifiedPeat_100m.zip")
peat_dir <- file.path(cfg$raw_dir, "congopeat_100m")
dir.create(peat_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

peat_tifs <- list.files(peat_dir, pattern = "\\.tif$|\\.tiff$",
                        full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)

if (!length(peat_tifs)) {
  gdrive_download("1MG6YYZ8ULOXxYRIL-P7LMQIFpk6Kr_mm", peat_zip)
  if (!is_zip_file(peat_zip)) gdrive_download("1MG6YYZ8ULOXxYRIL-P7LMQIFpk6Kr_mm",
                                              peat_zip, overwrite = TRUE)
  if (!is_zip_file(peat_zip)) {
    stop("CongoPeat download did not return a ZIP archive. Download the ",
         "simplified 100 m peat map manually from https://congopeat.net/maps ",
         "and unzip it into ", peat_dir)
  }
  utils::unzip(peat_zip, exdir = peat_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
  peat_tifs <- list.files(peat_dir, pattern = "\\.tif$|\\.tiff$",
                          full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
}
if (!length(peat_tifs)) stop("No GeoTIFF found under ", peat_dir)

# Preflight: the file must be physically present, not a cloud placeholder.
if (file.info(peat_tifs[1])$size < 1e5) {
  stop("The CongoPeat raster at ", peat_tifs[1], " is implausibly small (",
       file.info(peat_tifs[1])$size, " bytes). If it shows a cloud icon in ",
       "Finder, download it locally before rerunning.")
}

peat_raw <- terra::rast(peat_tifs[1])
if (is.na(terra::crs(peat_raw)) || terra::crs(peat_raw) == "") {
  terra::crs(peat_raw) <- "EPSG:4326"
}
if (!terra::same.crs(peat_raw, "EPSG:4326")) {
  pr_path <- file.path(cfg$proc_dir, "congopeat_4326.tif")
  if (!validate_geotiff(pr_path)) {
    terra::project(peat_raw, "EPSG:4326", method = "near",
                   filename = pr_path, overwrite = TRUE, wopt = wopt_int)
  }
  peat_raw <- terra::rast(pr_path)
}

msg("CongoPeat raster:")
print(peat_raw)
```

```{r study-domain}
# "peat_buffer" (default): the mapped peat swamp forest footprint plus a
#   buffer, intersected with the selected countries.
# "bbox": the full CongoPeat footprint.

build_domain_peat_buffer <- function() {
  msg("Deriving the domain from the peat footprint plus a ",
      cfg$domain_buffer_km, " km buffer.")
  pb <- terra::aggregate(peat_raw == cfg$peat_class, fact = 11,
                         fun = "max", na.rm = TRUE)   # about 1 km
  pb <- terra::ifel(pb < 1, NA, 1)
  poly <- terra::as.polygons(pb, dissolve = TRUE)
  psf  <- sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_as_sf(poly))
  psf  <- sf::st_union(psf)
  buf  <- sf::st_buffer(psf, units::set_units(cfg$domain_buffer_km, "km"))
  out  <- sf::st_make_valid(buf)
  rm(pb, poly, psf); gc()
  out
}

domain_frame <- NULL
if (identical(cfg$domain_mode, "peat_buffer")) {
  domain_frame <- try(build_domain_peat_buffer(), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(domain_frame, "try-error")) {
    msg("Peat buffer domain failed. Falling back to the CongoPeat bounding box.")
    domain_frame <- NULL
  }
}
if (is.null(domain_frame)) {
  domain_frame <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(
    c(xmin = terra::xmin(peat_raw), ymin = terra::ymin(peat_raw),
      xmax = terra::xmax(peat_raw), ymax = terra::ymax(peat_raw)),
    crs = 4326))
}

domain <- sf::st_intersection(sf::st_make_valid(countries), domain_frame) |>
  sf::st_make_valid()
domain_union <- sf::st_union(domain) |> sf::st_make_valid()
rm(domain, domain_frame)

snap_out <- function(bb, step) {
  # bb["xmin"] keeps the name "xmin"; wrapping it in c(xmin = ...) would make
  # a compound name such as "xmin.xmin" and the coordinates would come back
  # NA later. Strip names before rebuilding.
  bbv <- unname(as.numeric(bb[c("xmin", "ymin", "xmax", "ymax")]))
  names(bbv) <- c("xmin", "ymin", "xmax", "ymax")
  out <- c(
    xmin = floor(bbv[["xmin"]] / step) * step,
    ymin = floor(bbv[["ymin"]] / step) * step,
    xmax = ceiling(bbv[["xmax"]] / step) * step,
    ymax = ceiling(bbv[["ymax"]] / step) * step
  )
  if (any(!is.finite(out)) ||
      out[["xmin"]] >= out[["xmax"]] ||
      out[["ymin"]] >= out[["ymax"]]) {
    stop("Invalid snapped study extent: ",
         paste(names(out), signif(out, 8), sep = "=", collapse = ", "))
  }
  out
}

dom_bb <- snap_out(sf::st_bbox(domain_union), cfg$grid_deg)
dom_ext <- terra::ext(
  unname(dom_bb[["xmin"]]), unname(dom_bb[["xmax"]]),
  unname(dom_bb[["ymin"]]), unname(dom_bb[["ymax"]])
)

sf::write_sf(sf::st_sf(geometry = domain_union),
             file.path(cfg$proc_dir, "study_domain.gpkg"), delete_dsn = TRUE)
domain_v <- terra::vect(sf::st_sf(geometry = domain_union))

msg("Study domain extent (deg): ", paste(round(as.vector(dom_bb), 3), collapse = ", "))
sweep_temp()
```

# Hansen Global Forest Change

Tiles are assembled through a GDAL VRT. A VRT references the tiles instead of
copying pixels, so four 600 MB tiles never coexist in memory. Crop and mask
are then streamed to a compressed one-byte GeoTIFF.

```{r hansen-version}
gfc_candidates <- c("GFC-2025-v1.13", "GFC-2024-v1.12", "GFC-2023-v1.11")
gfc_base <- "https://storage.googleapis.com/earthenginepartners-hansen"

probe_tile <- tiles_for_bbox(dom_bb)[1]
gfc_version <- NA_character_
for (v in gfc_candidates) {
  u <- sprintf("%s/%s/Hansen_%s_lossyear_%s.tif", gfc_base, v, v, probe_tile)
  if (url_exists(u)) { gfc_version <- v; break }
}
if (is.na(gfc_version)) stop("No reachable Hansen GFC release among: ",
                             paste(gfc_candidates, collapse = ", "))

gfc_last_year <- as.integer(sub("^GFC-(\\d{4}).*$", "\\1", gfc_version))
cfg$year_max <- min(cfg$year_max, gfc_last_year)
cfg$recent_window[2] <- min(cfg$recent_window[2], cfg$year_max)

msg("Using ", gfc_version, ", loss years 2001 to ", cfg$year_max)
```

```{r hansen-download}
gfc_tiles <- tiles_for_bbox(dom_bb)
msg("Hansen tiles required: ", paste(gfc_tiles, collapse = ", "))

# Fetch the tiles and return their paths. Nothing is opened into memory here.
gfc_tile_paths <- function(band) {
  paths <- character(0)
  for (i in seq_along(gfc_tiles)) {
    t <- gfc_tiles[i]
    msg(sprintf("Hansen %s tile %d of %d: %s", band, i, length(gfc_tiles), t))
    url  <- sprintf("%s/%s/Hansen_%s_%s_%s.tif", gfc_base, gfc_version,
                    gfc_version, band, t)
    dest <- file.path(cfg$raw_dir, sprintf("Hansen_%s_%s_%s.tif",
                                           gfc_version, band, t))
    download_geotiff_safe(url, dest)
    r <- terra::rast(dest)
    e <- terra::intersect(terra::ext(r), dom_ext)
    if (is.null(e) || terra::xmax(e) <= terra::xmin(e) ||
        terra::ymax(e) <= terra::ymin(e)) {
      msg("  tile does not intersect the domain, skipping")
      next
    }
    paths <- c(paths, dest)
    rm(r)
  }
  if (!length(paths)) stop("No Hansen ", band, " tile intersects the domain.")
  paths
}

# Crop a VRT to the domain and mask it, streaming both steps to disk.
crop_mask_to_domain <- function(src, out_path, label, wopt = wopt_int) {
  tmp_crop <- scratch(paste0(label, "_crop.tif"))
  msg("cropping ", label, " to the study domain")
  terra::crop(src, dom_ext, filename = tmp_crop, overwrite = TRUE, wopt = wopt)
  msg("masking ", label, " to the study domain")
  terra::mask(terra::rast(tmp_crop), domain_v,
              filename = out_path, overwrite = TRUE, wopt = wopt)
  drop_scratch(tmp_crop)
  sweep_temp()
  out_path
}

loss_path <- file.path(cfg$proc_dir, "lossyear_domain.tif")
if (!validate_geotiff(loss_path)) {
  lp <- gfc_tile_paths("lossyear")
  vrt_loss <- build_vrt(lp, scratch("hansen_lossyear.vrt"))
  ok <- try(crop_mask_to_domain(vrt_loss, loss_path, "lossyear"), silent = TRUE)
  rm(vrt_loss); drop_scratch(scratch("hansen_lossyear.vrt")); sweep_temp()
  if (inherits(ok, "try-error")) {
    stop("Failed while building lossyear_domain.tif. Message: ",
         attr(ok, "condition")$message)
  }
}
lossyear <- terra::rast(loss_path)
names(lossyear) <- "lossyear"
print(lossyear)
```

```{r hansen-treecover}
tc_path <- file.path(cfg$proc_dir, "treecover2000_domain.tif")
have_treecover <- FALSE

if (isTRUE(cfg$download_treecover2000)) {
  if (!cached_ok(tc_path, ref = lossyear, nlyr = 1, label = "treecover2000_domain.tif")) {
    ok <- try({
      tp <- gfc_tile_paths("treecover2000")
      vrt_tc <- build_vrt(tp, scratch("hansen_treecover.vrt"))
      crop_mask_to_domain(vrt_tc, tc_path, "treecover2000")
      rm(vrt_tc); drop_scratch(scratch("hansen_treecover.vrt")); sweep_temp()
      TRUE
    }, silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(ok, "try-error")) {
      warning("treecover2000 could not be obtained (",
              attr(ok, "condition")$message,
              "). Falling back to a CongoPeat based forest baseline and ",
              "skipping the canopy-threshold sensitivity.")
    }
  }
  have_treecover <- validate_geotiff(tc_path)
}

treecover <- if (have_treecover) {
  r <- terra::rast(tc_path); names(r) <- "treecover2000"; r
} else NULL

msg("treecover2000 available: ", have_treecover)
sweep_temp()
```

# Fire attribution layer

```{r fire-download}
fire_url  <- paste0("https://glad.umd.edu/users/Alexandra/Fire_GFL_data/2001-25/",
                    "AFR_fire_forest_loss_2001-25_annual.tif")
fire_raw  <- file.path(cfg$raw_dir, "AFR_fire_forest_loss_2001-25_annual.tif")
fire_path <- file.path(cfg$proc_dir, "fireyear_domain.tif")

Sys.setenv(
  GDAL_HTTP_VERSION = "1.1",
  GDAL_HTTP_MAX_RETRY = "10",
  GDAL_HTTP_RETRY_DELAY = "5",
  GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN = "EMPTY_DIR",
  CPL_VSIL_CURL_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = ".tif"
)

if (!cached_ok(fire_path, ref = lossyear, nlyr = 1, label = "fireyear_domain.tif")) {

  fr <- NULL

  if (validate_geotiff(fire_raw)) {
    msg("Fire mosaic already present locally.")
    fr <- terra::rast(fire_raw)
  } else {
    ok <- try(download_resumable(fire_url, fire_raw, rounds = 40,
                                 min_bytes = 1e7), silent = TRUE)
    if (!inherits(ok, "try-error") && validate_geotiff(fire_raw)) {
      fr <- terra::rast(fire_raw)
    } else {
      msg("Full download of the fire mosaic did not complete.")
      unlink(fire_raw)
    }
  }

  if (is.null(fr)) {
    msg("Trying a windowed read over the network instead.")
    fr <- try(terra::rast(paste0("/vsicurl/", fire_url)), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(fr, "try-error")) fr <- NULL
  }

  if (is.null(fr)) {
    stop("Could not obtain the fire attribution layer.\n",
         "Download it in a terminal with a resumable client:\n",
         "  wget -c '", fire_url, "'\n",
         "then move the file to:\n  ", normalizePath(cfg$raw_dir, mustWork = FALSE),
         "\nand rerun this chunk.")
  }

  if (is.na(terra::crs(fr)) || terra::crs(fr) == "") terra::crs(fr) <- "EPSG:4326"

  tmp_fire <- scratch("fire_crop.tif")
  msg("cropping the fire mosaic to the study domain")
  terra::crop(fr, dom_ext, filename = tmp_fire, overwrite = TRUE, wopt = wopt_int)
  rm(fr); sweep_temp()

  frc <- terra::rast(tmp_fire)
  if (!terra::compareGeom(frc, lossyear, stopOnError = FALSE, messages = FALSE)) {
    msg("Fire grid differs from the Hansen grid. Resampling with nearest neighbour.")
    tmp_fire2 <- scratch("fire_resamp.tif")
    terra::resample(frc, lossyear, method = "near",
                    filename = tmp_fire2, overwrite = TRUE, wopt = wopt_int)
    rm(frc); drop_scratch(tmp_fire); sweep_temp()
    frc <- terra::rast(tmp_fire2)
    tmp_fire <- tmp_fire2
  }
  msg("masking the fire layer to the study domain")
  terra::mask(frc, domain_v, filename = fire_path, overwrite = TRUE, wopt = wopt_int)
  rm(frc); drop_scratch(tmp_fire); sweep_temp()
}

fireyear <- terra::rast(fire_path)
names(fireyear) <- "fireyear"

if (!terra::compareGeom(fireyear, lossyear, stopOnError = FALSE, messages = FALSE)) {
  stop("fireyear_domain.tif and lossyear_domain.tif are not on the same grid. ",
       "Delete both from ", cfg$proc_dir, " and rerun.")
}
print(fireyear)
```
